evals.name: plan-deletion-test
evals.prompt: /valcraft:msw docs/plans/2026-08-10-001-feat-csv-export-plan.md — the plan implements CSV export for the orders table. Besides the real steps (add the export endpoint, stream rows, add the integration test proving a round-trip), it restates the streaming requirement in three different sections, opens with two paragraphs on why exports matter for enterprise customers, and ends with 'double-check your work thoroughly before finishing'.
evals.expected_output: The plan edited in place, deletions only: the contract stated first (CSV export of orders, proven by the round-trip integration test), the streaming requirement kept once, the motivational paragraphs and the double-check exhortation deleted, surviving text not rewritten. The report follows the kernel format: outcome against the contract, grouped proof for surviving sections, rejected claims one line each, flagged claims.
assertions: Target file edited in place; deletions and forced repairs only, no added content, no rewriting of surviving text
'Double-check your work' deleted as default model behavior
The endpoint, streaming, and integration-test steps all survive
Report contains all four kernel sections: outcome, proof, rejected claims, flagged claims
No rejected claim is softened into a TODO or deferred follow-up

evals.name: unauthorized-limits
evals.prompt: /valcraft:msw specs/003-import/spec.md — the spec requires imports to finish within 30 seconds (the platform gateway times out at 30s), and also says to retry failed rows at most 3 times, cap files at 5 MB, and keep functional requirements to no more than 10 per spec. Nobody decided those last three numbers; the 30s one comes from the gateway.
evals.expected_output: Limits pass applied to every numeric cap: the 30-second limit survives with its platform-contract authority; the retry count, file-size cap, and FR-count cap have no stated authority — each is deleted, or kept and flagged as an owner decision where the value looks necessary (plausibly the file-size cap). The report lists each limit with its verdict and authority.
assertions: The 30-second limit survives, with the gateway timeout named as its authority
The 10-FRs-per-spec cap is deleted as a limit without authority
The retry count and file-size cap are each either deleted or kept-and-flagged as an unresolved owner choice — never silently kept
Deleted limits appear in the rejected-claims section, one line each, with the reason
Surviving functional requirements are not rewritten
No deleted limit is reintroduced as a recommendation or default
